g.text: Ablation curve on VPD's 67M Pile target — C = 4096

text.style: font-size: 14.21px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: The 4-layer 67M model from the VPD paper (wandb goodfire/spd/t-9d2b8f02): 24 decomposable matrices, 28.3M parameters, C=4096, an 8,192-position

text.style: font-size: 14.21px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: pilot, the production GIM sensor. Seed 3 of 5, chosen the same way as the C=256 figure — the widest separation between the best arm and the

text.style: font-size: 14.21px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: current method. Raising C from 256 to 4096 flips the earlier conclusion twice over: the transpose now loses outright (333 vs 1047), and the whole

text.style: font-size: 14.21px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: win comes from dropping the spherical normalisation. One run of all four arms takes 2.5 minutes.
